# nonRelative

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a relative path.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonRelative() — Checks whether a value is **not** a relative path. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonRelative(path: string): boolean;
```

`nonRelative(value)` is the same test as `!isRelative(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

The exact complement of `isAbsolute`: anything that does not start at a root, which includes the empty string.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description        |
| :-------- | :------- | :----------------- |
| `path`    | `string` | The path to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a relative path; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonRelative("/var/log"); // => true
nonRelative("https://example.com/a"); // => true
nonRelative("docs/readme.md"); // => false
nonRelative("./a"); // => false
nonRelative(""); // => false
```
